author: 1Jesus1GOD
title: A fun game buried underneath greed, repetition, and terrible balance
content:
Whiteout Survival starts out looking like a strategy game, but the longer you play, the more obvious it becomes that strategy takes a back seat to spending money.

The game constantly introduces events, heroes, upgrades, gear, charms, pets, chief equipment, and other systems designed to keep moving the goalposts. You can spend weeks saving resources and improving your account, only for someone willing to spend hundreds or thousands of dollars to completely overpower you.

State politics can make the experience even worse. A handful of powerful players or alliances can essentially control an entire state, and weaker or newer players have very little leverage if leadership becomes toxic. Instead of building a civilization and surviving the frozen wilderness, you can end up spending more time dealing with alliance drama, NAP rules, event schedules, and whales than actually enjoying the game.

The gameplay also becomes painfully repetitive. Gather resources. Train troops. Upgrade buildings. Wait on timers. Do Bear Trap. Do Crazy Joe. Do Foundry. Do Frostfire. Save for SvS. Repeat. Eventually it feels less like playing a strategy game and more like maintaining a second job that keeps asking for your credit card.

The monetization is relentless. There is always another pack, another limited-time offer, another progression system, and another reason you’re supposedly falling behind. The difference between free-to-play players and heavy spenders can become ridiculous.

The most frustrating part is that there actually IS a good game underneath all of this. The alliance system can be fun, coordinating events with other players can be enjoyable, and building your city initially feels rewarding. But the game takes those good ideas and surrounds them with excessive monetization, repetitive chores, enormous power gaps, and nonstop pressure to keep up.

If you want a casual survival strategy game, understand what you’re getting into. This game can consume an unbelievable amount of time while constantly reminding you that somebody with a bigger wallet can erase months of your progress advantage.

Whiteout Survival isn’t really about surviving the cold. It’s about surviving the monetization and politics . Remember that real hard earned money spent in this game can and will be used and taken away in a heartbeat from a moderator of that state your assigned . Moderators that are at the top tier of the highest alliances . Essentially you’re putting your money in the hands of a Korean owned game/app and Korean moderators choose to use you until they cannot advance any further and they kick you from their alliance no matter how much that you contributed! I doubt anyone will ever see this but If it does make it to a top review there are very much perverts sending inappropriate messages to individuals that are in other countries. Be aware !

title: Same thing over and over
content:
Whiteout Survival has a cool concept, but it’s extremely poorly executed. There’s very little actual enjoyment in completing meaningless tasks that are built around doing the same repetitive things over and over.

The game feels heavily designed around getting players to spend real money just to keep progressing, and honestly, I can’t see any reason why a simple phone game like this is worth spending real money on. The graphics are mediocre, the gameplay becomes repetitive very quickly, and much of the experience feels like repeating the same tasks indefinitely.

Spending money to keep doing the same thing over and over doesn’t make the game more enjoyable—it just makes the grind more expensive.

That’s pretty much the definition of insanity: doing the same thing repeatedly and expecting a different result.

Cool idea, poor execution, excessive repetition, and not worth spending real money on. 
The creators also require a nickname for your review and if it’s below what they want they won’t let you use any nickname to write the review. Zero stars now

Bottom line: pay-to-win mechanics, frequent bugs, and support that treats you like a suspect instead of a customer. Not worth the download.

author: AltairGardens
title: Too many things with not enough individual ability to advance
content:
How are we supposed to advance to a level 4 in the alliance?  I can’t contribute or collect anything without being a level 4, and it appears that NOBODY in this group is advanced except the leader.  

If it’s something I need to do, please educate me so I can follow through.  

If the leader is supposed to be creating advancement for everyone, please educate me about on how to approach this issue. 

This one issue is costing me advancement in other areas of the game as well.  

Help!?

Also, having to wait DAYS! For something to upgrade after completing the upgrade tasks is really ridiculous.  You HAVE TO BUY time advancements if you want to continue the game without waiting days to complete a building upgrade.  Seriously!?  It’s like the developers want us all to find a different game to play while we wait.  

So why play this game if we can’t play this game whenever we want to?   Seems like a no brainer to me, but apparently they don’t need or want more dedicated players.  

I’m about ready to uninstall this just from frustration.  Also, the guided instructions end way too quickly to catch on to how to play.  I have literally just gone back-and-forth to a building and looked at the lists for upgrades and done those, because it’s not clear on what I’m actually supposed to do in the game. 

Maybe before letting the guided instructions end create an input option for the layers to keep it going until we completely understand what we’re supposed to be doing, and in what order.  

If asked, I would have opted to have the instructions continue.

I’ve spent way too much money in this game without getting much satisfaction at all.

Building upgrades have a timer and you can only upgrade one at a time unless you spend money/gems.  Here is a question - why are we trying to heat the outside air?
